questions.prompt: Which list names factors the lesson says affect membrane fluidity?

options.a: Fatty acid saturation, fatty acid chain length, temperature, and cholesterol
options.b: Carbohydrate chains, the glycocalyx, self recognition, and non-self recognition
options.c: Cholesterol only, because it is the only membrane component mentioned
options.d: Fatty acid saturation, fatty acid chain length, temperature, and glycocalyx

questions.prompt: Which statement best reflects that fluidity depends on more than one factor?

options.a: Temperature affects membrane fluidity; saturation and chain length do not.
options.b: Saturation affects membrane fluidity; temperature and chain length do not.
options.c: Temperature, saturation and chain length can each affect membrane fluidity.
options.d: Chain length affects membrane fluidity; temperature and saturation do not.

questions.prompt: A student says cholesterol always makes membranes stiffer. Which correction fits the lesson?

options.a: It increases movement when very fluid and prevents stiffening when cold.
options.b: It restrains movement when very fluid and prevents stiffening when cold.
options.c: It restrains movement when very fluid and promotes stiffening when cold.
options.d: It increases movement when very fluid and promotes stiffening when cold.

questions.prompt: A membrane becomes very fluid. What is cholesterol's likely effect?

options.a: It increases the movement of membrane components
options.b: It stops all movement of membrane components
options.c: It makes the membrane stiffen further
options.d: It restrains excessive movement of membrane components

questions.prompt: Membranes with cholesterol stay usably flexible across a wider temperature range. Which explains this?

options.a: It restrains movement when very fluid and prevents stiffening when cold.
options.b: It increases movement when very fluid and prevents stiffening when cold.
options.c: It restrains movement when very fluid and promotes stiffening when cold.
options.d: It increases movement when very fluid and promotes stiffening when cold.

questions.prompt: Cell 1 has intact carbohydrate chains on its outer surface, while cell 2 lacks them. Which prediction fits the lesson?

options.a: Cell 2 is better equipped to recognize other cells
options.b: Both cells are equally able to recognize other cells
options.c: Cell 1 is better equipped to recognize other cells
options.d: Neither cell is able to recognize other cells

questions.prompt: A student says the glycocalyx is inside the cell and controls fluidity. Which correction fits the lesson?

options.a: It is a sugar coating on the inner surface that helps cells recognize each other.
options.b: It is a sugar coating on the outer surface that helps cells recognize each other.
options.c: It is a sugar coating on the outer surface that controls how membrane components move.
options.d: It is a sugar coating on the inner surface that controls how membrane components move.

questions.prompt: Two cells meet. Which description connects the glycocalyx’s location with its role in that encounter?

options.a: Sugar chains on their outer surfaces help control membrane movement.
options.b: Sugar chains on their inner surfaces help them recognize each other.
options.c: Sugar chains on their inner surfaces help control membrane movement.
options.d: Sugar chains on their outer surfaces help them recognize each other.

questions.prompt: Two membranes have identical cholesterol but different fatty acid chain lengths. Does this alone guarantee equal fluidity?

options.a: Yes, because cholesterol alone sets fluidity
options.b: No, because chain length is a listed factor that can change fluidity
options.c: Yes, because chain length has no effect on fluidity
options.d: No, because only temperature can change fluidity

questions.prompt: Membrane P has cholesterol, and membrane Q lacks it. Both are cold, and all other fluidity factors are the same. Which is expected to remain more flexible?

options.a: Membrane Q, because cholesterol makes cold membranes stiffer
options.b: Both equally, because cholesterol matters only when warm
options.c: Membrane Q, because cholesterol restrains movement in cold membranes
options.d: Membrane P, because cholesterol helps prevent stiffening when cold

answer_key.rationale: The lesson lists saturation, chain length, temperature, and cholesterol as factors affecting fluidity.
The lesson says fluidity depends on more than one factor, including saturation and chain length.
Cholesterol restrains movement when very fluid and helps prevent stiffening when cold, per the lesson.
The lesson says cholesterol restrains excessive movement when the membrane is very fluid.
Cholesterol restrains excessive movement in a very fluid membrane and helps prevent stiffening in the cold.
The sugar coating helps cells recognize each other and tell self from non-self, so intact chains favor cell 1.
The glycocalyx is a sugar coating on the outer surface that helps cells recognize each other.
The glycocalyx consists of carbohydrate chains on the outer surface and helps cells recognize each other.
Chain length is a listed factor affecting fluidity, so identical cholesterol alone does not guarantee equal fluidity.
With all other fluidity factors the same, membrane P is expected to remain more flexible because cholesterol helps prevent stiffening when cold.
